title: Inverse-surface anchor token set for compact components (night-weight)
creator: Aria Patel
description: Deliver a tightly-scoped token set and component overrides to anchor brand accents and interactive affordances in the console's compact density mode for night / dark themes. This ticket covers: mapping new inverse-surface tokens, hover/pressed motion-safe elevation tokens for small buttons and chips, chart stroke and legend adaptations to preserve brand contrast, and a lightweight override strategy so enterprise brand variants can be applied without breaking accessibility. Purpose: reduce visual drift across branded accounts while keeping contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for body text and >= 3:1 for interactive iconography where possible.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Token spec published in Figma + Confluence and synced to design tokens repo; 2) Small button, chip, table-row, chart-line visuals updated in component library storybook and pass visual QA; 3) Automated contrast checks added to token CI for night themes; 4) Engineering has an implementation plan with fallback behavior for legacy brand overrides; 5) PM sign-off on customer-visible changes and rollout plan.
decisions: - Use an 'inverse-surface-anchored' set instead of adding more brand-specific tokens to minimize combinatorial explosion; - Chart strokes will use a semi-opaque brand tint over a neutral stroke to preserve hue while meeting contrast; - Small interactive elevations will be expressed as overlay tokens (overlay-01, overlay-02) rather than shadow-heavy elevations to ensure consistent rendering in VMs and on lower-end GPUs; - Brand overrides will be limited to color anchors and not change spacing or iconography.
token_mapping_examples: inverse-surface-anchored-01 -> neutral-900 @ 88% alpha over surface-900; button-compact-bg-accent -> brand-primary-tint-30 over inverse-surface-anchored-02; chip-outline -> mix(brand-primary, neutral-700, 32%); chart-line-brand -> brand-primary at 92% with stroke-width 1.5px (compact).
outstanding_risks: - Some partner brand palettes with shallow contrast may fail automated checks; need to surface remediation guidance. - Existing customer CSS overrides in older Private installs could conflict with overlay token strategy. - Potential performance differences on older GPUs when using semi-opaque overlays in canvas-rendered charts.
test_plan: 1) Run token contrast CI for 25 representative brand palettes (provided by Solutions Eng); 2) Visual regression across standard pages in compact density (buttons, table rows, chips, charts); 3) Accessibility audit (AXE + manual keyboard focus) focusing on interactive icon contrast; 4) Smoke deploy to staging with feature-flagged rollout.
rollout_notes: Feature-flag rollout per customer tier: internal beta -> opt-in for 10% of accounts -> broader opt-in -> default on for new tenants. Provide migration guide for Dedicated/Private customers explaining CSS override patterns to avoid. Communicate in release notes and in-console update with a preview toggle for customers to compare old vs new tokens.
